title: A seal records the components its run reached
intention: When the tester seals a proof, the seal records which other components the run actually reached (by import, or by a python subprocess) and the seal state each was in, so a later move there can be seen from here.
traces_to: Law 9 via 1b6516f92db3 and parent 50e0581737e8. Law 3: reach is measured at runtime, never inferred from a static closure, which misses subprocess reach (the measured 5bc3 -> verdict-siblings case).
how: (a) cairn/devices/tester/reach/sitecustomize.py: when os.environ has CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG, register an atexit that appends json.dumps({'pid': os.getpid(), 'files': sorted(m.__file__ for m in sys.modules.values() if under the cairn root)}) + newline to that path. Then chain-load the next sitecustomize on sys.path after this dir with importlib.util. It must import nothing from cairn (cairn/__init__.py stays import-free). (b) In _subject_env, prepend the reach dir to PYTHONPATH and set CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG to runs.run_dir(test)/reached.jsonl. (c) At seal (~700-735), read the JSONL, map each file through grammar.component_of on its repo-relative path, drop unmapped files and the proof's own component, and set evidence['reached'] = {dir: validation_store.seal_digest(dir)} sorted by dir. (d) Proof at the path above, four teeth, PROVES keyed on this ticket, run under --netns.
falsifier: Done when cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_records_what_it_reached.py is green under bin/cairn test --netns. (1) A fixture proof that imports cairn.tools.validation_store seals with that component's dir in evidence.reached, valued at its seal_digest. (2) A fixture proof whose subprocess runs `python -m` on a module of another component carries that component too. (3) A fixture proof that reaches nothing outside its own component carries reached == {}. (4) The shadowed system sitecustomize still runs (a marker it sets is visible in the child). (5) A meta-proof that runs proof P via a python subprocess expires when P changes: P's file is in the meta-proof seal's fingerprint_closure, so a commit that changes only P re-runs the meta-proof at reseal instead of reading it settled. Measured 2026-10-13: 06f0445e7a63's anchor proof was repaired at 9c4f587a and its 3 meta-proofs (test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py, test_the_hollow_measures_the_repaired_build.py, test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py) stayed settled-red. Red at HEAD 4b3ac7f5: no reach dir, no evidence.reached.
why: Parent 50e0581737e8 needs each seal to say which components its run reached and in what seal state. Only the tester sees the run, so the recording is the tester's (RULE 1). A static closure misses subprocess reach, the measured first instance.

decisions.text: A python subprocess's loaded closure is unioned into the parent seal's fingerprint_closure, not only into evidence.reached — one capture mechanism gives both, so a meta-proof that runs proof P expires when P changes (clause 5). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.

map each logged file to its component with cairn.tools.base.address.component_of(path, pkg_root=<the proof's tree root>/cairn) — it returns the deepest owning component dir or None; grammar.component_of takes component names, not file paths, and returns None for a file

the reach log is a host tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='cairn-tester-reach-') beside closure_out, not run_dir: run_dir sits under the instance root the instance seal swaps out, so a log there is discarded with the swap; the tester reads it at seal and removes it
the proof seals plainly (isolation='none'): --netns is retired (ticket d80360545e91, exits 2), so no tooth relies on network isolation

evidence.reached = {repo-relative component dir: seal_digest(abs dir)}, sorted by key; drop files no component owns and the proof's own component; reached rides inside evidence (the eight ratified fields stand); a missing or unreadable log, or a moved tree, leaves reached unset and the existing fallback runs

two files: create cairn/devices/tester/reach/sitecustomize.py (atexit appends {pid, files} to $CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG, then exec the next sitecustomize.py on sys.path past its own dir); edit TesterDevice.run_proof in cairn/devices/tester/device.py — there is no _subject_env: the subject env is run_env = {**pinned, TEST_ID_ENV: test}, so add the reach dir to its PYTHONPATH and the log path there, and at the seal block (where _read_closure(closure_out, ...) is called) union the logged files into the closure and set evidence['reached']. The proof is already committed: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_records_what_it_reached.py, five PROVES-keyed teeth run by print_teeth_main, each sealing a committed fixture via TesterDevice().run_proof(fixture, sink='none', isolation='none'); the build does not touch it

measured on disk 2026-11-02: closure_out is the host tempfile.mkstemp path run_proof hands _CLOSURE_RUNNER, which dumps the subject's sys.modules __file__s there at exit; _read_closure(path, proof_path) turns that raw list into evidence['fingerprint_closure'] via validation_store.repo_relative_closure (repo-relative .py files the proof's component owns) — union the reach files into that same raw list before filtering; validation_store.seal_digest(component_dir) exists in cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py (ticket f43b5705ea03, PROVED); component_of(path, pkg_root) exists in the file cairn/tools/base/address.py at line 434, imported as from cairn.tools.base.address import component_of
